scenes.headline: Error Handling & Exceptions
scenes.subtitle: Failing gracefully in production pipelines
scenes.narration: Data jobs fail in messy, unpredictable ways, so good exception handling is what keeps a pipeline resilient instead of crashing silently in the middle of the night.

scenes.headline: The try/except lifecycle
scenes.narration: The try block wraps the code that might fail, and if an exception is raised, control jumps to a matching except clause. The else block runs only when the try body completed without error, keeping your happy path cleanly separated. And finally always runs regardless of outcome, which makes it the ideal place for cleanup like closing files or releasing connections.

scenes.headline: Catch specific, not everything
scenes.narration: Here raise_for_status turns any bad HTTP status into an exception we can catch. We handle a timeout separately from an HTTP error, because each deserves a different response and a different log message. By catching the narrowest exception type we can actually handle, real bugs still surface loudly instead of being silently swallowed by a broad catch-all.

scenes.headline: Best practices
items: Add custom exception classes for domain errors
Log the traceback, don't just print
scenes.narration: A bare except swallows everything including typos and keyboard interrupts, so it hides the very bugs you need to see. Using raise from links a new exception to its underlying cause, preserving the chain that explains what really happened. Custom exception classes give your domain errors names that callers can catch precisely. And logging the full traceback rather than printing means the failure is still diagnosable weeks later.

scenes.headline: Custom exceptions
scenes.narration: A small exception hierarchy makes error handling expressive. Callers can catch PipelineError to trap anything your pipeline raises, or catch RowValidationError to react to just that one precise failure. Passing the offending row id into the message turns a vague crash into an actionable, self-describing error.

scenes.text: Catch specific exceptions, log the traceback, and re-raise with `raise ... from` to keep the chain.
scenes.narration: Handle only what you can genuinely recover from, and let everything else propagate upward with its full context intact.
